title: Spec-Kit → Linear Bridge
lede: Your repository's spec-kit feature folders, mirrored into Linear as living, trackable issues — automatically, one way, and never by hand.

sections.title: What this system is
sections.subtitle: The one-paragraph version, then the why.

blocks.prose: This system is a spec-kit extension: install it into a repository, and every feature folder is reflected into Linear — one Project per repository, one Issue per feature, one sub-issue per implementation phase — and it keeps that reflection current automatically as you work.

source_refs.name: constitution · Principles I–II
source_refs.anchor: Filesystem is the single source of truth

blocks.prose: The filesystem is the single source of truth for planned work; Linear is a faithful projection of it. The bridge converges that projection to the files on every run — idempotently and without silently destroying information.

sections.title: Architecture at a glance
sections.subtitle: A reconcile engine over the filesystem, writing into Linear.

blocks.prose: The reconciler reads the repository, computes what Linear should contain, and makes it so. It is what every local trigger runs.

blocks.prose: State lives in exactly three inspectable places: the repository's filesystem, Linear itself, and the GitHub Action's per-run environment. There is no database, no daemon, and no local "last-seen" cache — the reconciler recomputes everything from the filesystem each run.

sections.title: Authority & safety model
sections.subtitle: Who wins when the repository and Linear disagree.

blocks.prose: The governing principle is that the filesystem is the authority. When the repository and a Linear issue disagree, the repository wins — but the bridge will not regress Linear blindly.

nodes.caption: Every write path begins here.

nodes.caption: The drift check decides whether Linear ranks higher than disk.

nodes.label: write silently
nodes.caption: No drift — forward / equal movement writes idempotently.

nodes.label: surface a structured warning
nodes.caption: Backward-drift — surface it; let the operator decide.

blocks.prose: The original rule was a hard gate tied to git branches: only a worktree on a feature's own branch could write it. It was superseded by the drift-aware model: any worktree may write, and the bridge detects and surfaces a backward move rather than forbidding it.
If an entire implementation phase is removed from tasks.md, what becomes of the sub-issue it created is not specified at all — neither cleanup nor retention is defined.

Backward-drift fires when Linear's recorded phase rank strictly exceeds the disk-inferred rank — clock-independent. A corroborating recency signal uses the feature folder's last git-commit time, never file mtime, with a small clock-skew tolerance.

blocks.prose: The core never knows what a "spec" is — every source becomes a uniform, source-typed corpus.
